title: OM Crosses Rs 100 Crore Worldwide, a First for Mammootty and a Sixth for Dhanush
excerpt: Rajkumar Periasamy's Tamil spy thriller O.M: Operation Mole reached Rs 104.58 crore worldwide in six days, even as daily collections fell from an Rs 18.1 crore opening day.
body:
• O.M: Operation Mole, Rajkumar Periasamy's Tamil spy thriller starring Dhanush, Mammootty and Sai Pallavi, crossed Rs 100 crore worldwide in six days, reaching Rs 104.58 crore.
  • It is Dhanush's sixth film to gross Rs 100 crore worldwide and the first of Mammootty's career, passing his previous best, Bheeshma Parvam (Rs 88.5 crore).
  • The film opened strongly at Rs 18.1 crore net in India but has declined every day since, earning Rs 4.1 crore on day six; its India net total stands at Rs 65.95 crore.
  • OM released on November 20 head-to-head with Dulquer Salmaan's Telugu film Aakasamlo Oka Tara — the first time father Mammootty and son Dulquer have had releases on the same day.

The Tamil film O.M: Operation Mole has crossed Rs 100 crore at the worldwide box office in its first six days. The spy action thriller, directed by Rajkumar Periasamy, stars Dhanush as an undercover police officer who infiltrates a red sandalwood smuggling ring, with Mammootty as the man running the ring and Sai Pallavi as a senior police officer. The cast also includes Naseeruddin Shah, Indrans and Sree Leela. The film is in Tamil, with Telugu and Hindi versions also playing, and it is inspired by real-life smuggling incidents.

The numbers, day by day

According to the tracker figures published by Koimoi, OM opened at Rs 18.1 crore net in India, then collected Rs 16.25 crore on day two and Rs 15.9 crore on day three, before dropping to Rs 6.2 crore on day four, Rs 5.4 crore on day five and Rs 4.1 crore on its first Wednesday. That takes the six-day India net to Rs 65.95 crore and the India gross to Rs 77.83 crore. Overseas collections of Rs 26.75 crore bring the worldwide total to Rs 104.58 crore. Koimoi attributes the slide after the opening weekend in part to mixed audience response. Tracker estimates vary slightly between outlets; The Hollywood Reporter India, citing Sacnilk, put the India net at Rs 61.45 crore as of November 25.

A first for Mammootty, a sixth for Dhanush

The milestone means different things for its two stars. For Dhanush, OM is his sixth worldwide Rs 100-crore grosser, after Thiruchitrambalam (Rs 117.88 crore), Vaathi (Rs 116.2 crore), Raayan (Rs 155.35 crore), Kuberaa (Rs 138.86 crore) and Tere Ishk Mein (Rs 164 crore). For Mammootty, it is the first Rs 100-crore film of his career: his previous highest grosser was the Malayalam film Bheeshma Parvam at Rs 88.5 crore worldwide. OM also returns Mammootty to Tamil cinema for the first time since Peranbu in 2018. The harder test is still ahead: Koimoi reports the film was made on a budget of Rs 200 crore, which would make it the most expensive film of both actors' careers, and the daily decline since the weekend leaves its final total uncertain.

The father-son clash

OM's November 20 release put it in direct competition with Aakasamlo Oka Tara, the Telugu film led by Mammootty's son Dulquer Salmaan — the first time the two have had films open on the same day. Aakasamlo Oka Tara, directed by Pavan Sadineni, has grossed about Rs 32 crore worldwide, according to Sacnilk figures reported by The Hollywood Reporter India. At a promotional event in Kochi, Dulquer played down the clash: "We have a big whale coming along with us. 'Om'. But both are films of different genres and in two different languages. Watch that one and this one too."

OM is currently playing in theatres; no streaming release has been announced in the coverage so far.
